newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Bardot, ex-husband fight book war.
newsitem.headline: France's Bardot, ex-husband fight book war.

text.p: France's former sex symbol Brigitte Bardot on Friday fired the second shot in a bitter literary battle with actor ex-husband Jacques Charrier, asking a court to order large cuts in a book he wrote about their marriage.
Bardot's lawyers requested description of their intimate life, love letters she once wrote to him, and pictures of her to be deleted from Charrier's book "My Reply to BB".
They also sought to halt the sale of the book, which was published last week, until the deletions were made about the actress-turned-animal-rights-campaigner.
Charrier, who was Bardot's husband from 1959 to 1963, called her a sexual "tease" in the book, written in response to her best-selling memoirs "Initiales BB".
Bardot, 62, had described him as "a vulgar, dictatorial and uncontrolled macho, a gigolo, alcoholic and despicable" and their baby as "a tumour feeding off me".
Charrier and his son Nicolas, now 36, failed to have Bardot's memoirs excised of 80 pages mentioning them. But a court awarded them 250,000 francs ($43,000) in damages.
